documents.unit: AI Governance Working Group / Information Technology
documents.title: Guidelines and Starting Points (Institutional Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI Tools)
documents.summary: Campus-wide IT guidelines from the AI Governance Working Group focused on data protection, responsibility for AI content, copyright, ethics and environmental impact. Teaching and learning rules are left to faculty, and students must follow instructor guidance.
documents.stance_why: The page says "guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty. Students are required to abide by faculty guidance", so it sets no student AI-use stance itself and delegates to instructors.

units.why: The opening line says IT "supports the responsible use and experimentation with generative AI tools", an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56 with unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: supports the responsible use and experimentation with generative AI tools

units.why: The preamble says the guidelines rest on "mission, values, and vision" and on environmental, intellectual and equitable commitments; it states principles for the framework, so P56 and not P53, which covers specific harms.
units.anchor: mission, values, and vision are the foundation of these guidelines

units.why: The sentence says the guidelines "support AI understanding, experimentation, and use across the College", giving scope and purpose of the framework (P56); it welcomes use, so permit.
units.anchor: support AI understanding, experimentation, and use across the College

units.why: "guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty" hands teaching decisions to faculty, which is P04 (instructor sets the rule); informs because it describes who decides.
units.anchor: guidelines specific to teaching and learning uses are the purview of Bowdoin faculty

units.why: "Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses" binds students to instructor rules; P04 fits (rules come from faculty) rather than P29, which is about owning submitted work.
units.anchor: Students are required to abide by faculty guidance for their courses

units.why: "you should only enter information available to the general public into generative AI tools" is a data-protection rule for all users, P50; it limits use, so restrict.
units.anchor: you should only enter information available to the general public into generative AI tools

units.why: The warning that default-setting input "is not private and could expose proprietary or sensitive information" explains why data must be protected, a P50 rationale.
units.anchor: Information shared with generative AI tools using default settings is not private

units.why: "Exceptions ... can only be made when using AI tools approved and explicitly documented by the Chief Information Officer" prefers vetted tools for non-public data, P50; restrict.
units.anchor: AI tools approved and explicitly documented by the Chief Information Officer (CIO)

units.why: "You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes AI-generated material" makes users own what they publish, P29; the accuracy warning is coded separately.
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish

units.why: "AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated" says output may be wrong, the P31 verify-output theme under the heading "Review AI content carefully".
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated

units.why: The note that AI content "may contain copyrighted material" flags an IP risk, so P52 and not P31 (accuracy).
units.anchor: may contain copyrighted material

units.why: "Faculty should be clear and explicit about their policies on generative AI" tells instructors to state AI expectations to students, P09.
units.anchor: should be clear and explicit about their policies on generative AI

units.why: "Students are encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed" is the ask-when-unsure rule, P10.
units.anchor: encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies

units.why: The pointer to teaching-and-learning AI resources for faculty in Canvas is faculty support material, P63.
units.anchor: Generative AI resources focused on learning and teaching can be found

units.why: "AI tools currently available at Bowdoin that are free to access with your bowdoin.edu account" describes college-provided sanctioned tools, P17 (also an access point, but provision fits P17 best).
units.anchor: AI tools currently available at Bowdoin that are free to access

units.why: "tools procured on behalf of the College are reviewed by IT and have the appropriate privacy, accessibility, and security protections" is institutional vetting of AI purchases, P65.
units.anchor: tools procured on behalf of the College are reviewed by IT

units.why: "Let us know if you have procured, are considering procuring ... generative AI tools" asks staff to report procurement to IT, part of vendor review (P65).
units.anchor: Let us know if you have procured, are considering procuring

units.why: IT workshops and LinkedIn Learning self-paced AI courses support people in learning AI; the closest type is P44 (building AI skills), and P63 does not fit as it is faculty-specific.
units.anchor: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Self-paced Training Courses, Linkedin Learning

units.why: "Academic dishonesty, in or out of the classroom ... constitutes a violation of the Academic Honor Code" classes dishonesty as an Honor Code violation under the heading to follow integrity policies; P36 (integrity process), neutral since AI is not named.
units.anchor: constitutes a violation of the Academic Honor Code

units.why: "Integrity is essential in creating an academic environment dedicated to the development of independent modes of learning" gives the learning rationale for integrity; P41 fits best.
units.anchor: dedicated to the development of independent modes of learning

units.why: "Restricted data should not be used with AI tools" is a flat ban on a data class, P50; prohibit for that data.
units.anchor: Restricted data should not be used with AI tools

units.why: "Sensitive data should be used with caution" is a conditional data rule from the Data Classification Policy, P50; restrict.
units.anchor: Sensitive data should be used with caution

units.why: The instruction to "Contact the person who stewards the data" before using it follows the Data Governance Committee practices, a data-protection process under P50.
units.anchor: Contact the person who stewards the data you are using

units.why: The warning that generative AI "has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams" with advice to report phishing is a cybersecurity rule; P53 covers ethical harms, not security threats, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Generative AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated scams
units.uncovered_note: Be alert for AI-enabled phishing and report suspicious messages; a cybersecurity rule not covered by any type.

units.why: "Please consider the environmental impact of AI models and available alternatives before using these tools" is an environmental concern that nudges less use, P53; restrict.
units.anchor: consider the environmental impact of AI models and available alternatives

units.why: "Aim to use AI tools and services that prioritize more sustainable models" is an environmental tool-choice recommendation, P53.
units.anchor: Aim to use AI tools and services that prioritize more sustainable models

units.why: "Clarify who holds the rights to content generated by AI tools" concerns ownership of AI output, P52.
units.anchor: Clarify who holds the rights to content generated by AI tools

units.why: "Ensure that output from AI tools do not infringe on existing copyright" requires avoiding copyright infringement in output, P52.
units.anchor: Ensure that output from AI tools do not infringe on existing copyright

units.why: "proper attribution or licensing agreements may be required" for AI content from copyrighted data is a licensing note, P52 and not P24 (student disclosure).
units.anchor: proper attribution or licensing agreements may be required

units.why: "Make clear when AI tools are being used in content creation or decision-making processes" requires openness about AI use, P24; the audience is stakeholders or the public.
units.anchor: Make clear when AI tools are being used in content creation

units.why: "Monitor and mitigate biases in AI outputs" is a bias and fairness duty, P53.
units.anchor: Monitor and mitigate biases in AI outputs

units.why: "Confirm that any images or videos generated by AI tools are free from copyright issues" is an IP rule for AI media, P52.
units.anchor: Confirm that any images or videos generated by AI tools are free

units.why: "Be cautious when using AI to generate or alter images and videos" warns about deepfakes and misrepresentation, an ethical harm, P53.
units.anchor: Be cautious when using AI to generate or alter images and videos

units.why: "ensure that personal privacy is respected, and obtain consent where applicable" for AI images of people protects privacy, P50.
units.anchor: ensure that personal privacy is respected, and obtain consent where applicable

notes: Single included document; guidelines address all users, so most units have actor all.
